brief: Eric Peters (One River) relays Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's press remarks describing a solid, resilient economy: strong productivity, robust capital investment, and unemployment little changed, offered as justification for the Fed having 'removed a dose of accommodation' (a rate cut). Warsh gives three reasons long-term yields rose since the last FOMC meeting: economic strength, hyperscalers competing for capital in funding markets, and geopolitics, specifically Ukraine's attacks on Russian refining capacity and Strait congestion pushing up crack spreads and energy prices. Peters argues Warsh omitted a fourth reason: the government cannot control chronic deficit spending without a recession that could lift the deficit from 6% of GDP to 13% or more. He casts Warsh's three reasons as long-term positives or transitory, but says only the deficit reason would spark a sharp yield spike, and bond vigilantes must judge whether that time has come. Treasury Secretary Bessent is buying bonds to push yields lower; Peters says this only works if wars end and productivity keeps rising, not if the world loses faith in US creditworthiness. 10yr yields sit at 5%, 30yr at 5.33%.
